result.builder:
Goal: add a --shout flag to the greet CLI (issue https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12). The pull request must meet every one of these lines:
1. node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
2. without --shout the output is unchanged
3. docs/index.md documents --shout
4. after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. bin/greet.js currently takes the first argument that does not start with '--' as the name and prints greeting(name) followed by a newline.
2. In bin/greet.js, detect '--shout' anywhere in process.argv.slice(2). When it is present, print the same greeting converted to upper case (for example `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`). It should work before or after the name. Keep the name selection, the usage message and exit status 2 for a missing name as they are.
3. Leave the output without --shout exactly as it is now, byte for byte (for example `node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints `Hello, Ada!` and a newline). Do not change what greeting() returns for existing callers. If you add a helper or an option to src/greet.js, keep its default behaviour the same.
4. Add tests in test/greet.test.js (node:test) that run bin/greet.js as a child process: one with --shout showing upper-case output, and one without it showing the unchanged `Hello, <name>!` output. Run `npm test` and make sure every test passes.
5. Update docs/index.md so it documents --shout: show the usage (for example `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>`) and say that it prints the greeting in upper case. Keep the existing documentation for the plain form.
6. Line 4 can only be seen after merge. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes the docs/ directory to GitHub Pages on every push to main, so the docs/index.md change from step 5 is what produces it. Do not change pages.yml or move the docs out of docs/. Do not try to deploy or check the live site.
7. Open one pull request with these changes and link the issue in it.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for issue https://github.com/o/greet-cli/issues/12 at its head commit. Run each check below in order, one per expect line, and report PASS or FAIL for each one with the evidence you saw (commands and their output).

Setup: check out the PR head. Run `npm test` once and record the result. It is context only and is not a check.

Check 1. Expect line: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js --shout bob`. Also run `node bin/greet.js Ada` to get the normal greeting for comparison.
PASS: each --shout run prints the greeting in upper case, meaning the normal greeting text with every letter upper-cased (for example `HELLO, ADA!`).
FAIL: either --shout run prints lower-case or mixed-case greeting text, prints no greeting, or errors out.

Check 2. Expect line: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Get the base version: `git merge-base HEAD origin/HEAD` (or the PR's base commit), and check it out in a separate worktree, e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/greet-base <base-sha>`. Run `node bin/greet.js Ada`, `node bin/greet.js bob` and `node bin/greet.js` (no name) both at the base and at the PR head. Compare stdout, and for the no-name run compare stderr too.
PASS: for every one of these invocations, the head output is the same as the base output (the base prints `Hello, Ada!` for Ada).
FAIL: any of these invocations prints different output at the head than at the base.

Check 3. Expect line: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Read docs/index.md at the head, e.g. `git show HEAD:docs/index.md`.
PASS: the file mentions --shout and says what it does (that it makes the greeting upper case / louder) or shows how to use it.
FAIL: the file does not mention --shout, or mentions it without any description or usage.

Check 4. Expect line: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
The live result can only be seen after merge. Do not fetch or read the live page. Check what the head contains that will produce it: read .github/workflows/pages.yml at the head and confirm it still deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main and publishes the docs directory, and confirm that docs/index.md at the head (the file the workflow publishes as the page) contains --shout.
PASS: at the head, the Pages workflow still publishes docs/ on push to main and docs/index.md lists --shout, so the published page will list --shout once merged.
FAIL: the workflow no longer publishes docs/ (or was removed or changed so it would not deploy on push to main), or the file it publishes does not contain --shout.

Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL):
- Exact expected strings: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` → `HELLO, ADA!` plus a newline; `node bin/greet.js Ada` → `Hello, Ada!` plus a newline; flag after the name (`node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`) should also shout.
- The no-name usage message and exit status 2 should be unchanged; compare exit statuses between base and head.
- Note whether `npm test` passes and whether the new tests cover both the --shout and plain paths.
- Note whether src/greet.js greeting() still returns the same value for existing callers.
